newsitem.title: GERMANY: Most Germans not pleased Kohl will run again.
newsitem.headline: Most Germans not pleased Kohl will run again.

text.p: Most Germans do not believe Chancellor Helmut Kohl should stand for election again next year, according to a poll taken just after he announced he would seek another term and released on Friday.

According to the survey, carried out on Thursday by the Infratest group for WDR regional television, 53 percent of respondents said Kohl should not stand again, 34 percent said he should and 13 percent were indifferent or did not respond.

Kohl, 67, made the announcement in a television interview, ending months of speculation that, after over 14 years in charge, he might not have the appetite to tackle Germany's mounting economic and social problems in a record fifth term.

Forty percent of respondents said they thought Kohl's candidacy would tend to harm the prospects of his Christian Democrats (CDU) in the general election, due in late 1998, while 37 percent said it would boost the CDU's performance.
Asked who they thought was the best person to tackle Germany's current problems, just 25 percent of the 1,000 people polled named Kohl.
Thirty-one percent came out in favour of Lower Saxony state premier Gerhard Schroeder of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and 16 percent favoured SPD party chairman Oskar Lafontaine.
The SPD has yet to name its candidate for the chancellery but is likely to face a choice between the left-leaning Lafontaine and the more business-friendly Schroeder.

Schroeder regularly rates in polls as the man with the best chance of unseating Kohl but is treated with suspicion by SPD members for frequently ignoring the party line, for instance by suggesting European monetary union could be postponed.
Asked who the SPD should nominate, 59 percent of respondents named Schroeder and 23 percent Lafontaine. Among SPD supporters, 61 percent wanted Schroeder and 30 percent Lafontaine.
The Infratest survey confirmed a growing opinion poll lead in recent weeks for a combination of SPD and environmentalist Greens over Kohl's coalition of CDU and liberal Free Democrats.
In the poll, the CDU stood at 35 percent and the FDP at five percent while the SPD scored 40 percent and the Greens 12 percent.
There was little sign that Kohl's candidacy had boosted the CDU's rating, which was up just one point from an Infratest poll taken on March 13.
